bottom_line: In patients with a recent acute coronary syndrome, rivaroxaban vs placebo reduced the primary composite of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke (hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 0.96).
implications: These data support that, versus placebo, adding rivaroxaban after a recent acute coronary syndrome reduced the composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke (8.9% vs 10.7%; hazard ratio 0.84; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.96) while increasing TIMI major bleeding not related to CABG (2.1% vs 0.6%) and intracranial hemorrhage (0.6% vs 0.2%), with no significant difference in fatal bleeding (0.3% vs 0.2%, P = 0.66). The document also reports that the 2.5-mg twice-daily dose reduced cardiovascular and all-cause mortality versus placebo, whereas the 5-mg twice-daily dose did not show this survival benefit.

major_points.text: Double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial with 15,526 patients assigned to rivaroxaban 2.5 mg BID, rivaroxaban 5 mg BID, or placebo.
major_points.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, we randomly assigned 15,526 patients with a recent acute coronary syndrome to receive twice-daily doses of either 2.5 mg or 5 mg of rivaroxaban or placebo

major_points.text: Primary efficacy endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke.

major_points.text: Rivaroxaban reduced the primary endpoint vs placebo (8.9% vs 10.7%; HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.74 to 0.96; P=0.008).
major_points.quote: Rivaroxaban significantly reduced the primary efficacy end point, as compared with placebo, with respective rates of 8.9% and 10.7% (hazard ratio in the rivaroxaban group, 0.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 0.96; P = 0.008)

major_points.text: Both rivaroxaban doses reduced the primary endpoint vs placebo.
major_points.quote: with significant improvement for both the twice-daily 2.5-mg dose (9.1% vs. 10.7%, P = 0.02) and the twice-daily 5-mg dose (8.8% vs. 10.7%, P = 0.03).

major_points.text: The 2.5 mg twice-daily dose reduced cardiovascular death and all-cause death vs placebo; this survival benefit was not seen with 5 mg twice daily.
major_points.quote: The twice-daily 2.5-mg dose of rivaroxaban reduced the rates of death from cardiovascular causes (2.7% vs. 4.1%, P = 0.002) and from any cause (2.9% vs. 4.5%, P = 0.002), a survival benefit that was not seen with the twice-daily 5-mg dose.

major_points.text: Rivaroxaban increased major bleeding not related to CABG and intracranial hemorrhage vs placebo, without a significant increase in fatal bleeding.
major_points.quote: As compared with placebo, rivaroxaban increased the rates of major bleeding not related to coronary-artery bypass grafting (2.1% vs. 0.6%, P<0.001) and intracranial hemorrhage (0.6% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.009), without a significant increase in fatal bleeding (0.3% vs. 0.2%, P = 0.66)

inclusion_criteria.text: Patients under 55 years of age required diabetes mellitus or previous myocardial infarction in addition to the index event.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients who were under 55 years of age had either diabetes mellitus or a previous myocardial infarction in addition to the index event.
